description: Committee recommends $1 million loan to TCU Place.
Funds new theatre sound system over 10 years.
Loan at 4.153% interest, $30,600 quarterly payments.

chips.text: Loan helps TCU Place maintain $3.8 million reserves for flexibility.

description: Recommends $3.8 million loan for 2950 Lorne Avenue works yard.
Loan repaid through the utility.
Council should approve interim parking lot at 52 - 25th Street East.
Upgrades would cost $150,000 from capital project P.01420.
Lot could generate $50,000 net revenue annually.

chips.text: Addresses off-street parking demand in the 25th Street East area.

description: City will audit procurement processes for efficiency.
Audit explores using group purchasing organizations.
It will review existing procurement controls.

chips.text: Councillor Jeffries hopes the audit finds financial savings for the city.
Saskatoon taxpayers could see financial savings from the audit.
Uncertainty remains if Canoe Procurement will share necessary pricing information.

description: City to purchase land from St. Thomas More and St. Andrew's Colleges.
For College Drive Bus Rapid Transit widening.
Total $848,700, already in BRT project budget.

chips.text: Councillor Piers confirmed purchase cost is within existing BRT budget.

description: Approves a 2-year, 1-month lease for a Coming Home Centre.
Provides culturally appropriate space for Indigenous women, girls, two-spirits.
Annual cost is $69,000, funded by capital project.

chips.text: Councillors questioned if city should host, suggesting partnerships.
Parking stalls are for community members using the centre.
Administration will report on centre's benefits for 2028-2029 budget.

description: Leases 17.5 acres of commercial land in Aspen Ridge.
Generates approximately $1 million annually for the city.
This is a long-term lease, not a sale.

chips.text: Councillor praised 'outside the box' thinking for long-term financial sustainability.
This land lease approach is 'outside of what we normally do' for land development.

description: Items 6.3.1 to 6.3.5 detail five information reports.
Saskatoon Land reported $96 million sales, $28.8 million net earnings in 2025.
Land sales supported winter warming centers and housing for unhoused.
City works to ensure future land supply for housing development.

chips.text: Councillor Tapp questioned if concept plan approvals could be accelerated.
Celine Anger stated a report on the Homewood concept plan will come to Council this month.

description: City Auditor's 2025 annual report details office activities.
Report includes whistleblower hotline usage information.

chips.text: City Auditor clarified whistleblower reports include HR-related employee performance issues.
City employees use the whistleblower complaint line.

description: City administration updated finance committee on outstanding tasks and timelines.
City administration to report on strengthening internal audit function.
Recommendations include dedicated audit committee, more staff, whistleblower program.

chips.text: Chamber of Commerce supports increased auditor funding, believing it will pay for itself.
Saskatoon spends $1.42 per person on city auditor, below peer average of $2.30.
Greater Saskatoon Chamber of Commerce presented recommendations for city audit improvements.

description: Saskatoon approved a Land Matter.
